sources.title: Installation
sources.finding: Kiro documents distinct IDE, CLI, Web, iOS early access and Crew installations, with OS-specific requirements.

sources.title: Mobile
sources.finding: Kiro iOS is early access through TestFlight; detailed mobile documentation is still pending.

sources.title: Specs
sources.locator: Capability matrix; core structure; task execution
sources.finding: Specs create requirements/design/tasks files and schedule independent tasks in dependency waves; correctness testing and mobile parity have explicit limits.

sources.title: Cloud sessions
sources.locator: How sessions work; prerequisites; client matrix
sources.finding: Clients attach to the same remote session; disconnection does not stop work, approvals wait, and paid plans include cloud compute with a ten-session cap.

sources.title: Kiro Web
sources.finding: Web is a paid-plan cloud client with interactive, Spec and autonomous modes, cron schedules and a documented no-auto-merge boundary.

sources.title: Steering
sources.finding: Workspace and global steering have separate scopes; cloud use of local personal configuration requires opt-in upload.

sources.title: Crew quick start
sources.finding: Crew is a distinct local or user-hosted Gateway agent with persistent sessions, schedules, memory and a task runner.

sources.title: Local command sandbox
sources.finding: Kiro's optional local sandbox covers shell commands/children and optionally stdio MCP, excluding the agent and built-in file tools.

sources.title: Privacy and security
sources.finding: Supervised mode reviews file changes after writes and can revert them; it is explicitly not a security boundary.

sources.title: Kiro pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards; pooling; trial FAQ checked 7 November 2026
sources.finding: Free has fifty credits; paid individual tiers and pooled team seats differ in included credits. Add-ons cost $0.04/credit and taxes are excluded.

sources.title: Crew Agent Backends
sources.finding: Developer Mode enables Preview selection of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other harnesses. Existing sessions retain their backend. Pi lacks Crew MCP tools; Codex requires sandboxing; Claude preapproved calls may bypass Crew audit.

sources.title: Crew Task Runner
sources.locator: Loop; Task IDs; Recovery; Approval gates; Dependencies
sources.finding: Crew decomposes Markdown specs into persistent task runs and step sessions. Up to three runs/parallel steps, per-run IDs/branches/worktrees, test/review/retry checkpoints, restart reconciliation and explicit approval gates are documented.

sources.title: Requirements-First Specs
sources.finding: Kiro generates requirements.md with acceptance criteria, design.md with architecture and testing strategy, and tasks.md with dependencies and optional/required work. Humans review and refine each phase.

sources.title: Analyze Requirements
sources.finding: IDE/CLI requirements analysis identifies logical contradictions, ambiguities, conflicting constraints and missing cases. Chat answers update requirements.md. Web does not yet offer this analysis.

sources.title: Kiro Memory
sources.finding: Memory is stored locally per user account and shared by IDE/CLI on the machine. It defaults off in IDE and has read-only/learn controls. Current subagents can read parent memory but cannot modify it.

sources.title: Kiro Data Protection
sources.finding: Individual/free usage may supply content for improvement by default. IDE/CLI telemetry and content have separate opt-outs. Enterprise improvement collection is off; admin reports remain separately controlled. Free inputs may be held up to sixty days for abuse detection.

sources.title: Kiro License
sources.finding: Kiro IDE and CLI are AWS Content under AWS agreements and the AWS IP License. Chromium is the IDE engine; Bun powers the CLI frontend. Dependency licenses do not license the main application as open source.

sources.title: Crew Running 24/7
sources.finding: Crew Gateway can run as a service or in Docker on user hardware, including an always-on remote Linux host while the laptop sleeps. Sandbox availability is checked before container agent execution.

sources.title: Kiro Authentication
sources.finding: IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile support IAM Identity Center or organization identity providers such as Okta/Entra. CLI also has a CI/headless API-key path.

sources.title: Kiro Privacy and Security
sources.finding: IDE supervised mode presents agent file changes for human review and approval, but is explicitly not a sandbox or access-control boundary.

sources.title: Kiro Mobile availability
sources.finding: Android is publicly available through Google Play for Android 10+. iPhone requires requested early access through TestFlight; the request page says only limited invitees receive access. Both use paid-plan cloud sessions.

sources.title: Crew phone browser access
sources.locator: Reach it from a laptop or phone; named HTTPS tunnel; lines 236-433
sources.finding: The shipped gateway documents opening its HTTPS dashboard URL on a phone, including a named tunnel or Tailscale Serve token link. This is the user-hosted Crew browser client, distinct from the native Kiro Mobile app.

sources.title: Crew external harness authentication
sources.locator: AgentAuthDeclaration for Codex and Claude Code, lines 503-551
sources.finding: Codex uses its own .codex/auth.json and native sign-in; Claude Code uses its own .claude/.credentials.json and native terminal sign-in. Both are own_credential_file entitlements, independent of Crew Kiro logout. This establishes reuse of each coding agent account through its native harness rather than an API-key-only wrapper.

sources.title: Shared Crew human prompt admission
sources.locator: Chat prompt payload and admit_chat_turn; collab.py presence; attribution.py sender_line
sources.finding: Shipped chat admission records the verified actor with each prompt. The presence model distinguishes principals in one session and attribution labels multiple human authors in the same session. preview.py permits the owner to enable this released opt-in preview; this is distinct people sharing one Crew, not just same-account device access.

sources.title: Crew 0.12.0 release
sources.locator: November 5: More Coding Agents; Previews You Can Turn On
sources.finding: The public release removes Developer Mode, adds Strands and GitHub Copilot CLI, exposes provider keys in Settings Secrets, and ships Shared Crew as a preview owners can switch on to admit other people over Tailscale with equal access.

sources.title: Kiro harness architecture
sources.finding: The engineering explanation says the same standalone harness runs on a laptop or inside a VM in the cloud; remote clients connect to its cloud sandbox. This establishes VM execution, not tested containment guarantees.

sources.title: Kiro team administration
sources.locator: Teams; shared credit pools and enterprise controls
sources.finding: The complete pricing page distinguishes organization administrators who manage users, groups, pooled credit limits and access from assigned members. This establishes organization-level administrative roles, without claiming Crew fine-grained per-person roles from a proposal.

sources.title: Crew fixed native harness registry
sources.finding: The released runtime has a closed known-backend set for Kiro, Claude Code, KAS, Strands, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Goose, DeepSeek and Copilot. Registration rejects a backend outside that set. Edition plugin registration does not supply a generic arbitrary coding-harness adapter; configured MCP tool commands are a separate feature.
